reader_question: What does one family keep as its earnings rise and benefits phase out?
title: In this invented budget, a raise from $36,000 to $37,000 leaves a family $8,386 a year worse off, because its child care help ends.
reading_guide: The heavy line is what the family has after taxes and benefits, and the dashed line is its earnings alone. Where the heavy line drops, a raise leaves the family with less.
measure_line: What one invented family, a parent with two children in Alder County, has in a year after taxes and benefits, dollars, at earnings from $0 to $60,000 in steps of $1,000. Values and rules invented for this example.
notes: In this example, child care help worth $9,000 a year ends once earnings pass $36,000, while tax credits keep shrinking and taxes keep rising with each raise.
The family is back above what it had at $36,000 only when it earns $51,000.
Every rule here is invented. Real benefit cliffs depend on the state, the family and the year.
alt: Line chart of an invented family’s resources after taxes and benefits as its earnings rise from $0 to $60,000, beside a dashed line of earnings alone. Resources climb to $44,706 at $36,000 of earnings, drop to $36,320 at $37,000 when child care help ends, and pass $44,706 again only at $51,000.

table.caption: An invented family’s year, dollars, by earnings

chart_notes: Heavy line: resources after taxes and benefits. Dashed line: earnings alone. The light band runs from $36,000, where the drop comes, to $51,000, where the family is back above its $36,000 level. Both scales run from $0 to $60,000.

labels.cliff: Child care help ends above ${from_x}: ${drop} less at ${to_x}
labels.band: Below its ${from_x} level until earnings reach ${back_x}

notes_internal: Maker B, round 1. Data plan row 28, rule 14.42: the one illustrative specimen of rounds 1 and 2. The data file and sidecar are maker B's (brief), written by make_benefit_cliff.py in maker B's scratch folder; the sidecar's qualification states every invented rule, so the file can be rebuilt from it.

Checked by the script that writes the file: the largest drop is from $36,000 (resources $44,706) to $37,000 ($36,320), $8,386; resources first reach $44,706 or more again at $51,000 ($44,998). The form finds the same drop and climb back from the rows.

Rule 13.1: Illustration, with no grade line; Rule 13.8: 'Illustrative data' beside the chart, an invented place (Alder County) and generic benefit names (food aid, child care help, tax credits), so no real program's amounts are implied. H08: the title says 'invented budget' and states arithmetic on invented rules.
The dollar signs come through the label templates; R-B2 asks for a dollars format for the axes and table.
